sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year from FY2018 to FY2025, reaching $25.8 billion [F145][F8].

The path was a step change rather than a smooth climb: revenue jumped 22.3% in FY2022 to $23.0 billion [D131][F5], then fell 5.2% in FY2024 to $23.5 billion [D201][F7] before recovering 9.8% in FY2025 [D236].
The FY2024 decline reflected lower storm cost recovery revenues of about $1,090 million and lower fuel cost recovery revenues of about $526 million [P34].
The FY2025 rebound came from higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery [P21].
FPL remains the core, at 70.5% of FY2025 revenue [D271], and it contributed 5.5pp of the 9.8% revenue growth that year [D273][D236].
FPL's revenue increase was driven by higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan cost recovery revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery [P21].
Operating income grew 9.9% a year against 7.7% for revenue over the window [F146][F145], and in FY2025 operating costs grew 0.2pp faster than revenue [D257].
Net income compounded at only 0.4% a year and diluted EPS fell 0.7% a year [F147][F149], as the diluted share count rose 0.6% in FY2025 [D251].
The FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% [F24] sat above the 30.3% window median [D300] and well above the 25.7% utilities peer median [D311].
The largest move in the window was FY2023, when the operating margin rose 23.5pp to 41.3% [D177][F22], the window high [D299].
In FY2025 net margin of 26.5% [F40] sat 5.6pp below the 32.1% operating margin [F24], a gap of 5.6pp [D248].
The gap reflects other income (expense) of -$3,750 million [X64], including unfavorable non-qualifying hedge activity and higher average debt balances at Corporate and Other [P8].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion in FY2025 [F64] was 1.83x net income [D227], against a typical 2.11x in FY2021 [D87].
Operating cash flow was 48.4% of revenue in FY2025 [D225], down from 56.4% in FY2024 [D190].
The swing from a net over-recovery to a net under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by about $89 million in FY2025 [P19].
D&A ran at 25.5% of revenue in FY2025 [D224], and stock-based compensation was only 1.5% of operating cash flow [D228].
Total debt reached $95.0 billion in FY2025 [D230], leaving net debt of $92.2 billion [D231], or net cash of -357.4% of revenue [D232].
That net cash level ranks at the 0th percentile against utilities peers (n=4), whose median is -228.4% of revenue [D314][D315].
Long-term debt grew 18.8% a year over the window [F156], and the current ratio of 0.60x in FY2025 [F128] is the window high [D305].
Free cash flow was negative as investing outflows of $23.9 billion [F72] exceeded operating cash flow, while dividends paid were $4.68 billion [X82] and the share count rose 0.6% [D251].
The current ratio was 0.60x in FY2025, below 1.0x [F128][R1].
For a regulated utility with heavy capital spending, a sub-1.0x current ratio is a liquidity signal rather than a solvency one, given $2.81 billion of cash [F96].
Net cash fell for seven straight years, from -$34.3 billion in FY2018 [D9] to -$92.2 billion in FY2025 [D231][R2].
The steady debt build funds the renewable and grid investment programme, but it leaves the balance sheet the most levered in the peer group [D314].
The effective tax rate moved -23.3pp in FY2025, to -17.7% [D226][D191][R4].
The negative rate reflects clean energy tax credits at NEER [P11], so it flatters net income relative to operating profit and is unlikely to persist at this level.
Whether the FY2026 operating margin holds above the 30.3% window median [D300], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether net cash as a share of revenue improves from -357.4% [D232], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether operating cash flow to net income recovers toward the 2.11x FY2021 level [D87], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
